entities.summary: Paul LoicqFrench pronunciation: [lojk] was a Belgian lawyer, businessman and ice hockey player, coach, referee and administrator. He played ice hockey for Belgium men's national ice hockey team and won four bronze medals from in 1910 to 1914. He was a leading supporter of the efforts to introduce ice hockey at the Olympic Games, and served on the organizing committee for ice hockey at the 1920 Summer Olympics. After playing in the 1920 Olympics he served as president of the Royal Belgian Ice Hockey Federation from 1920 to 1935, and as president of the Ligue Internationale de Hockey sur Glace (LIHG) from 1922 to 1947, which was later known as the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Paul Loicq played a crucial role in introducing ice hockey to the Olympic Games and served as president of the Royal Belgian Ice Hockey Federation and the Ligue Internationale de Hockey sur Glace from 1920 to 1947, contributing to the development of international ice hockey.
